newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia steel hot as U.S. takes share spotlight.
newsitem.headline: Russia steel hot as U.S. takes share spotlight.

text.p: Record-breaking Wall Street stole investors' interest and left Russian shares quiet, with a few exceptions such as ferrous metals stocks, traders said on Friday forecasting a quiet market next week.

The Russian Trading System 22-share index ticked up to 364.78 from 363.96 on Wednesday, the previous day of trade, and just shy of the record 366.80 set on May 19. Volume was a miserly $21.0 million reported trade.
Traders said the ferrous metals sector was one of the best performers in first and second tier stocks. Nizhnetagilsky Metallurgichesky Kombinat rose to $0.118 from $0.115.
"It's not a transparent stock," said Alfa Capital trader Dmitry Lobanov. "But there's demand from all the big operators."
Western operators are generally seen reworking their portfolios to increase lesser known undervalued stocks.
Oil producer LUKoil rose to $15.72 at the close on a slew of late afternoon orders after $15.60 on Wednesday, traders said. Sberbank continued its rise, hitting $214.00 after $204.00.
National power company UES firmed to $0.3159 from $0.3155.
East European Investment Company senior trading manager Mikhail Osipov said rosy U.S. market prospects were keeping investors' attention.
"As long as it is interesting, (investors) will be be there," he said.
The Dow Jones index opened higher on Friday after Thursday's closing 7,711.47, its fifth straight record.
Menatep bank trader Sergei Kosynkin said he expected new fund flows to flow into the Russian market at volumes high enough to break RTS records at the end of the month.
The Russian market has usually been lifted in June by pre-holiday flows, he said.
